title: The canonical open/scalar adjoint comparison has the prescribed cochain normalization.
statement: For arbitrary commutative rings A and B, a ring homomorphism φ:A→B and an open immersion j:U→X, use the canonical comparisons of [lem-coef-etale-open-comparison-data] and [lem-coef-etale-hom-thick-locus]. The canonical q satisfies exactly OpenScalarExtensionNormalization φ j (openScalarExtension φ j), with no additional hypotheses.

proof.text: Regard the exact open localization factors as squares between the ordinary cochain adjunctions and the published derived open adjunctions. The unit formula for mapDerivedCategoryAdjunction on homotopy representatives, followed by the quotient factor identifications, shows that their right mates are precisely the inverse restriction localization factors. The scalar representative is the inverse mate of the corresponding scalar restriction localization factor, by its defining unit transpose. These are calculations for arbitrary complexes and require no K-flatness.

Form the two composite comparison squares, one through open extension then scalar extension and the other through scalar extension then open extension. Mathlib mateEquiv_hcomp identifies their right mates with the successive inverse exact restriction localization factors. The ordinary q-zero comparison is conjugate to the ordinary restriction/scalar square, degree by degree, using the unit-preserving uniqueness of left adjoints. The canonical derived q has the analogous conjugate by its definition.

The right restriction square commutes with localization factors: expand mapDerivedCategorySquareIso, apply the exact-functor composition and natural-isomorphism factorization equations, and cancel the factorization isomorphisms. Apply injectivity of mateEquiv, together with its two conjugation/whiskering laws, to obtain equality of the original composite left squares. Evaluating at any complex and identifying the scalar-square components with scalarExtensionRepresentative gives the required normalization equation. Restrict to the K-flat complexes in the original predicate.

Derived scalar extension commutes with extension by zero along an open immersion, normalized on K-flat complexes
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits including ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat, Module.Flat.baseChange and RingHom.Flat; no exact derived open normalization or mixed tensor theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleOpenExtensionNormalization
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] :
    OpenScalarExtensionNormalization φ j (openScalarExtension φ j)
